page_header: Histology and Anatomy of Flowering Plants · 4 marks

steps.label: What periderm is
steps.margin_note: One sentence for the meaning, then the three names as a short list.
lines: Periderm is the protective covering formed on
the outside of a dicot stem during secondary
growth.
Three layers taken together make the periderm:
cork (phellem),
cork cambium (phellogen), and
secondary cortex (phelloderm).
steps.why: The question asks what periderm is before it asks how it forms, so the three names must come first. Naming the three layers also fixes the order in which they are made.
common_mistakes: Writing that periderm is only the cork. Cork is one of its three layers.
Giving the English names without the technical ones. Phellem, phellogen and phelloderm are the marked words.
steps.memory_tip: Phellem, phellogen, phelloderm: outside, middle, inside.

steps.label: Why a new meristem is needed
steps.margin_note: Three short lines. This is the reasoning mark, so do not cut it.
lines: As the vascular cambium keeps dividing, the
stem grows in girth.
The epidermis and the outer cortex cannot
stretch any further, so they break and are
lost.
The stem now has no protective covering, so a
new meristem has to make one.
steps.why: Periderm exists because of a mechanical problem: the old covering was made for a thin stem and cannot grow with it. Stating that problem is what makes the rest of the answer reasoned rather than remembered.
common_mistakes: Skipping this step and starting with the cork cambium. The examiner looks for the reason.
Saying the epidermis stretches. It ruptures.
steps.memory_tip: The stem grows thicker than its old covering, so a new covering has to be made from inside.

steps.label: Cork cambium and its products
steps.margin_note: Two marks here. Name both products and say which side each is cut off on.
lines: A layer of cells in the cortex becomes
meristematic again. This new lateral meristem
is the cork cambium or phellogen.
The cork cambium divides and cuts off cells on
both of its sides.
Outer side: cork or phellem. Its walls are
thickened with suberin, so cork is impermeable
to water and gases and protects the stem.
Inner side: secondary cortex or phelloderm,
which is a living parenchymatous tissue.
steps.why: One meristem cutting off cells on two sides explains the whole structure in a single sentence: cork outside because that is where protection is needed, secondary cortex inside because that is where living tissue is needed.
common_mistakes: Saying the cork cambium makes cork only. It cuts off cells on both sides.
Writing phelloderm outside and phellem inside. Cork is always the outer product.
Leaving out suberin. It is the reason cork is waterproof.
steps.memory_tip: Phellogen is the middle layer, so it makes one product outward and one inward.

insider_note: The mark for periderm formation is lost most often by naming cork alone. Say clearly that the phellogen cuts off cells on both sides.
